diagnosis.notes: BASELINE: real unitrace counters on the single-pass online-softmax kernel (one work-group per Q row) showed GPU_BUSY ~100% but XVE_ACTIVE only ~2.66% and XVE_THREADS_OCCUPANCY_ALL only ~3.49% -- i.e. the GPU reports busy (dispatch/idle-wait overhead) while the vector engines are almost entirely unoccupied. Root cause: GQA decode shapes (nb=1, small nr23) launch only `nrows` work-groups total (nh=8 -> as few as 8 work-groups), far too few to fill a B70's execution units -- the same problem CUDA's fattn-vec.cuh solves via parallel_blocks/gridDim.y splitting ("flash-decoding"). A first hypothesis (removing a redundant barrier per KV iteration by having every work-item independently recompute the already-group-uniform softmax update instead of only lid==0 doing it) was tried and measured zero wall-clock change (2867.56 vs 2867.58 us) -- confirms barrier count was never the bottleneck; reverted. The kept fix (trial 2) splits the KV range into nsplit chunks per Q row so nrows*nsplit work-groups are launched instead of nrows, directly multiplying occupancy by nsplit (4/8/16x depending on shape), then merges the nsplit partial online-softmax states in a small second kernel. This is the standard flash-decoding technique. Occupancy improvement was not re-measured with HW counters after the fix (time-boxed to move to the next kernel) but is architecturally certain given the launch-count multiplier and is fully consistent with the observed speedup scaling with nsplit (nr23=[1,1]: nsplit=16 -> 15.0x; nr23=[4,1]: nsplit=8 -> 7.56x; nr23=[8,1]: nsplit=4 -> 3.85x).

trials.hypothesis: sycl::reduce_over_group already returns an identical value on every work-item, so the existing lid==0-computes-then-barrier-for-others-to-read pattern for the online-softmax rescale (scale_old/weight) is unnecessary; every work-item can independently recompute it in registers, removing 1 of 2 barriers per KV iteration.
trials.root_cause: No measurable change -- confirms the kernel is not barrier-bound; the real limiter is that decode shapes launch far too few work-groups (nh<=8) to occupy the GPU at all, so shaving one barrier per KV iteration inside each of those few work-groups has no effect on end-to-end time. Reverted via git checkout.

trials.hypothesis: Flash-decoding: split the KV range into nsplit chunks per Q row (launching nrows*nsplit work-groups instead of nrows) so decode shapes with few Q rows still fill the GPU; each split writes an unnormalized partial online-softmax state (m, l, acc[dv]) to a scratch buffer, then a second combine kernel (one work-group per row) merges the nsplit partial states redundantly per-thread (no barriers, nsplit is tiny) into the final normalized output. Heuristic (nrows<=64 and kv>=512, capped at 16-way split, >=256 KV positions/split) falls back to the original single-pass kernel for prefill/large-nrows shapes where occupancy is already fine.
trials.root_cause: Multiplying the work-group count by nsplit directly addresses the measured ~3.5% GPU occupancy at decode time. Speedup scales with nsplit as expected: nr23=[1,1] (nrows=8, nsplit=16): 2867.84->190.89 us (15.02x); nr23=[4,1] (nrows=32, nsplit=8): 2876.17->380.28 us (7.56x); nr23=[8,1] (nrows=64, nsplit=4): 2891.53->751.54 us (3.85x). Prefill shape (nb=4096, nrows>>64) unaffected -- heuristic selects nsplit=1 (fallback to unchanged original kernel), confirmed ~290-294 GFLOPS before and after, no regression.
